Set up the definite integral for the volume of revolution about the $x$-axis from $x = \frac{2}{3}$ to $x = 3$:
$$V = \pi \int_{2/3}^3 y^2\,dx = \pi \int_{2/3}^3 \left(2(3x - 1)^{-\frac{1}{3}}\right)^2 dx = 4\pi \int_{2/3}^3 (3x - 1)^{-\frac{2}{3}}\,dx$$

Integrate with respect to $x$ using the reverse chain rule:
$$V = 4\pi \left[ \frac{(3x - 1)^{\frac{1}{3}}}{\frac{1}{3} \times 3} \right]_{2/3}^3 = 4\pi \left[ (3x - 1)^{\frac{1}{3}} \right]_{2/3}^3$$

Evaluate at the upper limit $x = 3$ and lower limit $x = \frac{2}{3}$:
$$V = 4\pi \left[ (3(3) - 1)^{\frac{1}{3}} - \left(3\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) - 1\right)^{\frac{1}{3}} \right] = 4\pi \left[ 8^{\frac{1}{3}} - 1^{\frac{1}{3}} \right] = 4\pi(2 - 1) = 4\pi \quad (\approx 12.6)$$

ai_rubric.Volume of Revolution: Integrates $y^2$ to $4\pi(3x-1)^{1/3}$ (M1, A2). Applies limits $\frac{2}{3}$ to $3$ (DM1). Obtains exact volume $4\pi$ (A1).

Differentiate the curve equation with respect to $x$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 2\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)(3x - 1)^{-\frac{4}{3}}(3) = -2(3x - 1)^{-\frac{4}{3}}$$

Evaluate the coordinates and gradient at $A$ where $x = \frac{2}{3}$:
$$y_A = 2\left(3\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) - 1\right)^{-\frac{1}{3}} = 2(1)^{-\frac{1}{3}} = 2 \implies A = \left(\frac{2}{3}, 2\right)$$
$$m_T = \left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=2/3} = -2(1)^{-\frac{4}{3}} = -2$$
$$m_N = -\frac{1}{-2} = \frac{1}{2}$$

Write the equation of the normal line through $A\left(\frac{2}{3}, 2\right)$:
$$y - 2 = \frac{1}{2}\left(x - \frac{2}{3}\right) \implies y = \frac{1}{2}x - \frac{1}{3} + 2 \implies y = \frac{1}{2}x + \frac{5}{3}$$

ai_rubric.Equations of Normals: Differentiates to $-2(3x-1)^{-4/3}$ (B1). Evaluates $A(2/3, 2)$ and $m_T = -2$ (B2). Forms normal equation (M1). Obtains $y = \frac{1}{2}x + \frac{5}{3}$ (A1).
